title: The Crumb-and-Clover Exchange
premise: At a striped bakery stall, Mina wants to win the village’s ridiculous Golden Rolling Pin by making a treat everyone enjoys. Bramble the squirrel wants to trade his prized acorn-cup for something worthy of his grand pantry. Niko, Mina’s hungry neighbor, wants one honest snack after being told the stall is closed. Seed 893571092 determines which labels, tastes, and starting ownership make the day’s trouble bloom.
cast_and_props: Characters: Mina, an inventive child baker who wants a shared treat and the Golden Rolling Pin; Bramble, a proud squirrel who wants a grand trade and believes his acorn-cup is clearly labeled; Niko, a hungry neighbor who wants a fair snack and dislikes being treated like a beggar. Shared setting: one bakery exchange stall. Props: a tray of three buns, a flour-sack label, Bramble’s acorn-cup, a red ribbon, a Golden Rolling Pin prize card, and a small chalkboard. Declare every slot before scenes. Suggested entities: mina, bramble, niko, tray, bun_a, bun_b, bun_c, flour, cup, ribbon, prize, board. Keep all state scalar. Useful keys include mina.memes.welcome, mina.knows.tray.label, bramble.beliefs.cup.mark, niko.memes.hunger, niko.memes.pride, tray.owner, cup.owner, bun_a.taste, bun_b.taste, bun_c.taste, tray.label, board.message, mina.agrees.share, bramble.agrees.trade, niko.content, and prize.owner.
kernels_and_interactions: Use five kernel families. 1) Inspection and mistaken labels: observe lets characters learn the visible label or a bun’s actual taste, while beliefs remain stale until told. 2) Ownership and fair exchange: transfer moves the acorn-cup, ribbon, or chosen bun only when the current owner agrees; this creates different material endings. 3) Taste and making: Mina can combine declared ingredients or mark one bun sweet, salty, or clover-sour, but only after discovering which flour sack is which. 4) Invitation and agreement: tell shares a non-None belief; Mina can invite Niko, Bramble can offer a trade, and Niko can accept or refuse based on the snack and his pride. 5) Performance/prize: Mina presents a bun at the stall; the prize card changes owner only when the actual audience enjoys the result. Three distinct problems: (A) Mina reads the flour label correctly, but Bramble secretly swaps the red ribbon between sacks because he wants his clover bun to look grand; the resulting flavor is unexpectedly salty, forcing a trade or a comic rescue. (B) Bramble believes the tray’s star-marked bun is his promised reward, while Mina believes the star marks the stall’s best bun for Niko; their conflicting wants produce a tense ownership bargain rather than a repair task. (C) Niko arrives hungry but is mistaken for a critic because he carries the prize card he found outside; Mina performs a fancy tasting before him, while Niko wants a plain warm bun, producing either a welcoming exchange or a proud refusal. Reuse scenes for opening the flour sack, telling the truth about a mark, offering the acorn-cup, and presenting the final bun across all three problems.
seed_parameters: In build(seed), use random.Random(seed) to choose scalar initial facts, not routes. Seed-dependent premise keys should include tray.label (star/plain), flour.mark (sweet/salty), cup.owner (bramble or mina), and niko.arrival (hungry or carrying_prize). Suggested outcome keys: prize.owner, niko.content, cup.owner, tray.final_bun, and board.message. One seed may begin with the star bun promised to Bramble; another may begin with it promised to Niko. One may make Bramble’s cup already offered; another may make it guarded. One may give Niko the prize card, changing what Mina thinks he wants. The goal can accept several meaningful outcomes, such as niko.content == True or prize.owner == mina, but endings must distinguish a shared tasting, a completed trade, and a proudly rejected fancy bun. Use 12–22 scene/observe/tell/transfer candidates and aim for 5–10 selected events. Use 1–2 pivotal scenes only: Mina chooses to ask Niko’s taste, or Bramble admits the label swap. Include at least one Rule for a concrete agreement or completion, not an abstract counter.
candidate_scenes: Proposed candidate IDs and kernels: look_flour (observe, Mina learns flour.mark); look_tray (observe, Mina learns tray.label); look_cup (observe, Bramble learns cup.owner); notice_niko_card (observe, Mina learns niko.arrival); swap_ribbon (scene, Bramble changes flour.mark or ribbon.position when he wants a grand-looking bun); tell_label (tell, Bramble tells Mina his belief about the mark); ask_taste (tell, Mina tells Niko the available tastes and sets mina.agrees.share); plain_request (scene, Niko states niko.wants plain when hungry and not carrying_prize); choose_star (scene, Mina assigns tray.final_bun to bramble or niko according to her belief); offer_cup (scene, Bramble sets bramble.agrees.trade); trade_cup (transfer, Bramble gives cup for bun when offer and ownership conditions hold); bake_sweet (scene, Mina makes bun_a.taste sweet after flour discovery); bake_salty (scene, Mina makes bun_b.taste salty); bake_clover (scene, Mina makes bun_c.taste clover-sour); reveal_mark (scene, Mina learns or publicly changes board.message after a mistaken label); present_bun (scene, Mina gives the selected bun to Niko or Bramble); accept_snack (scene, Niko sets niko.content true when taste matches his want); reject_fancy (scene, Niko sets niko.content false and board.message to plain_is_best when offered an unwanted fancy bun); award_prize (scene, prize.owner becomes mina or niko when content and presentation conditions hold). Reuse look_flour, tell_label, offer_cup, trade_cup, present_bun, and the final shared-tasting bridge on materially different paths.
constraints: Return Python with build(seed) -> WorldSpec, importing only random and runtime symbols. Every state key must begin with an existing entity ID, and every slot must be declared in initial. Use C conditions with scalar constants only; never compare one state key to another. Use observe, tell, and transfer at least once. Guard transfers by actual owner, guard knowledge before claiming discoveries, and preserve stale beliefs until a tell or new observe. Effects must be atomic with no duplicate destinations. Do not use abstract counters or branch-number routing. Include catalog prose separately in the plan’s implementation: openings establish Mina’s actual desire and the seeded trouble; every candidate gets a scene card; endings are conditional on final prize.owner, niko.content, cup.owner, and board.message. Use phrase lexicon entries for every dynamic value mentioned. No card may claim a character knows a fact before an observe or tell. Keep the complete rendered story around 220–400 words, with two opening variants and two variants for each major ending. Bridges should connect routine baking without repeating debug summaries. The final image should show the stall’s changed arrangement—perhaps the Golden Rolling Pin holding down a plain bun, the acorn-cup brimming with crumbs, or an untouched fancy bun wearing a crooked red ribbon.
different_endings: 1) Shared welcome: Niko’s plain warm bun is accepted, Mina wins or shares the prize, and the last image is the Golden Rolling Pin used as a tiny table leg while three hands reach for crumbs. 2) Honest trade: Bramble receives the bun he truly wanted and transfers the acorn-cup; the cup becomes the stall’s new tasting bowl, its proud little rim dusted with sugar. 3) Tastefully ridiculous refusal: Niko rejects the fancy clover-sour bun, Mina learns to ask, and the abandoned bun becomes a hat for the prize card while Niko eats a plain roll nearby. 4) Bramble’s confession: the ribbon swap is revealed, but his cup is still offered fairly; the final image is the red ribbon tied around the cup instead of a flour sack, making the once-mistaken mark into a cheerful invitation. Each ending must be guarded by actual final state conditions and must not imply unused props or unperformed trades.
